records.summary: Scope and content: Original Caption: NEW ARMY FNGINEERS PRACTICE FOR SERVICE IN FRANCE. To get practical experience in the work they were later called upon to do when they arrived in France, men of the 101st Engineers, located in Boston, Mass., constructed roadbeds and laid street car tracks in the streets of Boston. Every forenoon a detail of 25 men and a lieutenant put in three hours of work. In the sections being laid by the men of the Engineer Regiment most of the work was done by hand in order that the men may get the experience. They already laid a two mile stretch of track on the Boston and Albany road between Westboro and North Grafton, Mass. The 101st Engineers was formerly the old crack command, the 1st Corps of Cadets, M.V.M. They recruited their ranks up to 3,000 men and 65 officers. Any opportunity to acquire added knowledge of field engineering was jumped at by the men who were enthusiastic over the prospect of service abroad. Photo shows men of the 101st Engineers using a pneumatic drill while tearing up an old car roadbed in Boston.

records.summary: Cemetery of fallen soldiers of the Polish Army in the battle of Tomaszów Lubelski on September 23, 1939, in Antoniówka in the Zamość region near Tomaszów Lubelski. Cemetery of fallen soldiers of the Polish Army in the fight against the German Nazi invaders in the Polish Defense War in September 1939 during World War II. The cemetery is located in Antoniówka. On the road from Zamość to Tomaszów Lubelski - in Budy - turn right. And then, in the village of Antoniówka, on the left side of the road, there is a cemetery of the Polish Army Soldiers who died in the Battle of Tomaszów Lubelski on September 23, 1939. A narrow path leads to it. Almost in front of the last house in this town. Almost 500 (five hundred) soldiers of the Polish Army who died in September 1939 in the Polish Defense War in the Second Battle of Tomaszów Lubelski during World War II are buried in the cemetery.

records.summary: Monument to the victims of the massacre of the villages of Huta Dzierążyńska and Budy on January 29, 1943, in the village of Huta Dzierążyńska in the Zamość region. It was a massacre perpetrated by Nazi Germans during World War II and the German occupation of defenseless Polish civilians. The Germans then murdered 50-80 people, including women and children. The monument also commemorates the fallen Polish soldiers in the vicinity of the village in the battle of Tomaszów Lubelski in September 1939 and fallen partisans of the Polish resistance against the German occupation in Poland 1939-1945. Polish villagers - victims of German concentration camps and prisons were also commemorated: Franciszek Chrzanowski was 40 years old, Maciuk Tadeusz was 18, Michał Posikata was 58 years old, Roczniak Franciszek was 30 years old, and Roczniak Jan was 57 years old.
